Executive summary

Credo reported its seventh straight quarter of triple-digit growth tonight: revenue of $479.0M (+115% YoY), non-GAAP EPS of $1.20, a Q2 guide of $525–535M that is ~3% above consensus, and a full-year outlook lifted from ">80%" to ">85%" growth with optical revenue guided above $600M (DSPs, silicon-photonics PICs and ZeroFlap transceivers each >$100M). Customer concentration eased again — the top customer is now 33% of revenue versus 67% for all of FY25 — and retimers, optical DSPs and PICs each posted records.

The stock nevertheless fell 8.65% into the print on 2× volume and another ~9% after hours to ~$188, roughly −17% over two sessions and −39% from the June 22 high. Three things explain the gap between the headline and the tape: (1) the beat cadence has collapsed — revenue beats of +12–17% a year ago are now +1–1.5% and the EPS beat was $0.03, so "beat-and-raise" is fully priced; (2) GAAP gross margin stepped down 370 bp to 64.5% and the Q2 GAAP GM guide (62.9–64.9%) confirms optics and acquired intangibles are structurally lower-margin than the AEC franchise; (3) the setup was already broken technically — lower high on Aug 17, MACD bearish cross on Aug 31, OBV distribution since June — while insiders sold $477M of stock in 12 months with zero purchases.

Our read. The business is compounding faster than any name in our AI-hardware coverage (FY26 +206%, FY27 guide >+85%, ~50% net margin), the optical pivot is now real revenue, and at ~$188 the stock trades at ~31× FY27E / ~21× FY28E non-GAAP EPS — cheaper than ALAB (44×) and MRVL (31×) on forward earnings despite faster growth. But 84% of revenue comes from four hyperscalers, the largest of which (Amazon, inferred) is still 33%, and the Street's $283 mean target was set with the stock at $230–300. We frame CRDO as a high-conviction business at a contested price: the $177 July swing low is the line that decides whether this is a violent range or a deeper reset toward the rising 200-day (~$175).

Management's FY27 math cross-checks: >85% growth ⇒ >$2.47B; ~50% non-GAAP net margin ⇒ ~$1.24B; on ~200M shares ⇒ ~$6.20 — essentially consensus. The FY28 debate is whether optical (PICs + ZeroFlap at "3-digit ASPs") and scale-up products (OmniConnect, Blue Heron, ALC) layer in fast enough to offset AEC reach shrinking to ~5 m at 200G/lane. Evercore's $325 target assumes AEC +60% in CY27 and 2028 EPS >$13; the bear case (24/7 Wall St, $196) assumes hyperscaler capex deceleration and a top-4 customer at 87% of revenue.

Watch for the first post-print revisions Wednesday. No analyst action had been published as of 9 pm ET. The tell will be whether Stifel ($350), BofA ($340) and JPM ($335) defend the optical thesis and whether Rosenblatt (Neutral, $215) cuts — the $184 Street-low target is the only one already below the after-hours price.

The valuation debate is about durability, not the multiple. On EV/TTM sales CRDO is second only to ALAB; on forward earnings it is cheaper than MRVL and ALAB because the Street underwrites >85% growth. That premium is contingent on (a) four hyperscalers not pausing simultaneously, (b) non-GAAP GM holding ~68% as optics goes to ~25% of revenue, and (c) FY28 scale-up products arriving on time. Bear pieces (Seeking Alpha "Detached-From-Reality Expectations", "Hidden Risks") focus on exactly those three plus insider selling.

08 · SWOT

SWOT analysis

Strengths

  • De-facto standard in AECs with an estimated ~85–90% share; qualified at five of six major hyperscalers; "one customer fully penetrated on all three swim lanes."
  • SerDes-first engineering delivers 7 m reach at ~half optics' power on a 12 nm "workhorse" node — cheaper wafers and a less contested foundry lane than 5/3 nm rivals.
  • Vertical integration: chip → cable system → PILOT telemetry / ZeroFlap link-health software. Hyperscalers qualify the system, creating a 6–9 month switching cost.
  • Financial model: 68% non-GAAP GM, 48% operating margin, ~50% net margin, FCF $407M in FY26, no debt; FY27 guide >85% growth.
  • Optical now real: DSPs, PICs (DustPhotonics) and ZeroFlap each guided >$100M in FY27; first two PIC wins exclude Credo DSPs — an upsell path.
  • Concentration improving: top customer 67% (FY25) → 33% (Q1 FY27); four >10% customers; neoclouds targeted at ~20% of revenue.

Weaknesses

  • 84% of revenue from four customers; the largest (Amazon, inferred) still 33%, second (xAI/Microsoft, inferred) 28%. A single pause moves a quarter.
  • GAAP margin erosion: GAAP GM 64.5% (−370 bp QoQ) and Q2 guide 62.9–64.9%; $93M GAAP/non-GAAP opex gap; SBC 13.7% of revenue.
  • Insider supply: $477M sold in 12 months, zero buys; founders' stakes −19–23%; D&O ownership 11.8% → 9.1%.
  • Dilution: share count +8.6% in 12 months (ATM, warrant, SBC, M&A); ~200M diluted next quarter; no buyback.
  • Working capital: inventory $313M (+$62M QoQ, DIO ~168 days) ahead of an H2 ramp that must arrive; FCF conversion fell to 35% of NG net income in Q1.
  • Product-line revenue not disclosed; AEC share of revenue can only be inferred; scale-up revenue is "essentially zero today."
  • Beta 3.2 and a post-M&A cash pile of $764M (from $1.44B) — less optionality for the next deal.

Opportunities

  • 1.6T / 200G-per-lane cycle (Vera Rubin first): ASP uplift "from 800G to 1.6T across the portfolio"; 1.6T AEC in H2 FY27, "a much bigger way" in FY28.
  • Scale-up networks (UALink / ESUN / NVLink-adjacent): Blue Heron 200G retimer, OmniConnect SerDes ("$2–3K per GPU" potential), Weaver gearbox, NPO via Open CPX MSA — all FY28 revenue.
  • Active LED cables (Hyperlume micro-LED, 10–30 m, "reliability of copper"): TAM management says is "more than double" AEC's; demo at OFC, revenue FY28.
  • Silicon photonics in-house: PIC market ~$6B by 2030 (LightCounting); "substantially fewer lasers" lowers ZeroFlap cost; sells into modules that don't use Credo DSPs.
  • Hyperscaler capex: 2026 top-4 guide $720–745B (~$835B with Oracle); Dell'Oro sees >$3T worldwide DC capex by 2030; neoclouds/model-builders ~60% CAGR.
  • Sixth hyperscaler (Google is the notable absence); PCIe Gen6 AECs to mass production in H1 FY27; TAM ">$10B", "3× larger than 18 months ago."

Threats

  • Marvell (sells AEC DSPs to Amphenol/Foxconn/Innolight-Recodeal at reportedly 15–20% lower prices; "AEC + retimer revenue to more than double in FY27") and Astera Labs (Taurus 800G/1.6T AECs ramping H2 2026, "$4B+ AEC TAM by 2030") — share loss and price compression.
  • Reach shrinkage: AEC max reach falls from ~7 m to ~5 m at 200G/lane, ceding row-scale links to optics; LPO removes the DSP from modules.
  • NVIDIA: passive copper cartridges inside NVL72/144 (no Credo content), Spectrum-X/Quantum-X Photonics CPO switches, $4B into Coherent/Lumentum; Rubin Ultra moves scale-up toward optics.
  • Customer capex digestion / ROI scrutiny (Alphabet Jul 28 sell-off); AWS Trainium cadence; any of the four could pause a rack generation.
  • Tariffs / Taiwan: 100% TSMC wafers; assembly and BizLink cable manufacturing in Asia; every guide caveated on the tariff regime.
  • Integration risk on ~$1.3B of acquisitions in 12 months (goodwill $986M); key-person risk as founders monetise; Zacks downgrade and Rosenblatt Neutral show the first cracks in a 18/1 Buy consensus.
09 · Competitors & technology

Who Credo competes with, and how the physics differs

Why AECs exist — the plain-English version

At 100G per lane, a passive copper cable (DAC) can only carry a clean signal about 2–3 metres before loss becomes unrecoverable, and the cable is thick. An active electrical cable puts a retimer/DSP chip in each connector that fully regenerates the signal: reach extends to ~7 m (≈5 m at 200G/lane), the cable is ~75% thinner, power is roughly half an optical transceiver's, price ~5–10% lower, and — because there are no lasers — link "flaps" are two orders of magnitude rarer. The cost is ~300 ns of latency, irrelevant for Ethernet scale-out. AECs win for GPU/NIC-to-top-of-rack, dual-ToR and rack-to-adjacent-rack links; they lose to optics beyond ~7–9 m (row-to-row, pod-to-pod) and to passive DAC/backplane inside a single rack (NVIDIA's NVL72 NVLink spine has no retimer content).

Where Credo's edge is — and isn't

Edge: purpose-built low-power SerDes (Credo began as a SerDes IP house) that hits the reach/power target on 12 nm where rivals need 5–7 nm; a complete system (chip + cable + firmware + PILOT telemetry) that hyperscalers qualify as one part; ZeroFlap link-health telemetry "up the stack"; and being first — five hyperscaler relationships with 6–9 month qualification cycles. Not an edge: price. Marvell reportedly sells AEC DSPs to cable integrators 15–20% below Credo, and Astera's Taurus undercuts on module price. Credo's counter is that hyperscalers buy reliability, not the cheapest retimer.

Substitution risk, ranked

  1. Reach shrinkage at 200G/lane (7 m → ~5 m) hands some rack-to-rack links to optics — Credo's answer is ZeroFlap optics + ALC (copper-like reliability to 30 m).
  2. Co-packaged optics on switches (Broadcom TH6-CPO, NVIDIA Photonics). LightCounting sees CPO viable "by 2028–29"; management: low-single-digit switch share through ~2029 until reliability/serviceability is "bulletproof." Credo joined Open CPX MSA for NPO.
  3. LPO / linear-drive removes the DSP from pluggables (hurts Credo/Marvell DSP revenue) — but ZeroFlap and PIC revenue are DSP-agnostic.
  4. NVIDIA rack design: scale-up stays passive copper in NVL72/144 (no Credo content) and moves to optics in Rubin Ultra; Credo's exposure is scale-out/front-end, which persists across GPU vendors.

Recurring themes worth quoting

AEC standard: "AECs are now the de facto standard for intra-rack and rack-to-rack connectivity up to 7 meters… We continue to believe the industry is early in its AEC adoption." (Q3 FY26)
Gross margin: long-term model "63–65%" was repeated through Q3 FY26 while actuals ran 67.6–68.6%; since June the framing is "broadly consistent with fiscal 26 levels" — the 63–65% model has been quietly retired but not formally replaced.
Scale-up: "the bulk of our revenue from AI is really in scale-out now; we don't have revenue in scale-up today." (Q3 FY26) — FY28 is when scale-up, ALC and OmniConnect layer in.
Reach: "max AEC reach at 200G per lane may decrease slightly from 7 meters to perhaps 5 meters." (Q3 FY26)
Supply: "significant tightness in the supply chain" but wafers (12/7/5/3 nm), lasers and cable capacity committed; Q1 FY27 inventory +$62M "leaning in" for H2.

Sector context

SOXX +104% and SMH +88% over 12 months versus CRDO +68% (Sep 1 close); the semis complex is 10–12% off July highs while the connectivity cohort is 9–20% off. iShares reports SOXX at a ~65× trailing P/E — CRDO's 82× trailing / ~31× forward sits inside that band on forward numbers. The demand driver is intact on paper (top-4 hyperscaler 2026 capex $720–745B; Dell'Oro's 2030 DC capex forecast nearly doubled since January to >$3T) but investors are now pricing capex ROI risk (Alphabet's Jul 28 sell-off), which compresses multiples for the picks-and-shovels names first. MSCI index membership and sector valuation aggregates could not be pulled this session (entitlement error); at ~$35–40B CRDO would ordinarily sit in MSCI USA standard, not Small Cap — unverified.
